To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The αβ interaction of the Escherichia coli trp operon-encoded tryptophan (Trp) synthase is essential for catalysis.
two residues, Val 126 and Val 128 in the α subunit of Escherichia coli TrpA, are important for interaction between the α and β subunits of the tryptophan biosynthetic enzyme, tryptophan synthatase.

two amino acid changes in the α subunit of tryptophanase are responsible for the loss of the ability of the α subunit to bind the β subunit, and that the intrinsic catalytic activity of the mutant α subunit was not significantly affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the specificity and mechanism of the αβ interaction.
the study of protein–protein interaction in the tryptophan biosynthetic enzyme, tryptophan synthatase (TS) from Escherichia coli.
the study of protein-protein interactions and how the structure of the protein complex is related to the function of the individual subunits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residues α66, α109 and α126 are important in the interaction between the αβ subunits.
the residues α126, 128, 109 and 118 are essential for the αβ interaction.
these mutations do not alter the overall structure of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the residues identified are not critical for αβ interaction.
the residues involved in the interaction of the αβ dimer are distributed across the whole length of the protein.

the non-interactive mutants are not simply the result of single point mutations, but that they are more complex and involve a number of residues, some of which are located on the surface of the α subunit, others in the interior, and some are close to the active site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the residues involved in non-interactive mutants are not clustered in one particular area of the molecule.
the αβ interface of tryptophanase is not as rigid as the interface of tryptathione synthase and that a single point mutation is sufficient to disrupt the interaction.

the residues identified as important in the interaction between the α and β subunits of tryptophan biosynthetic synthase are not conserved in the homologous α and β subunit of the tryptophanase enzyme.
